question: Before building any anti-detection work, two things had to be settled: (1) is there still a server-rendered Google results page, i.e. any route that needs no JavaScript, and (2) does the community evidence support 'session age / persistent cookies' as what gets past the check.

endpoint_matrix_curl_cffi_chrome150.verdict: JS shell, no results in HTML

community_evidence_against_the_session_a.claim: cookies lifted from a LOGGED-IN Google session used to return search results; as of 2026-07-25 that no longer works

a new header is set on every new search; JavaScript challenges run continuously to verify the page is being rendered by a real browser, not a headless script -- the same applies to a generated SG_SS cookie
outcomes are IP-related: two of his IPs started returning results while some proxy IPs still return none
Google are doing TLS inspection; the Nokia UA works again only via curl_cffi impersonating chrome99_android -- measured dead from every egress we own on 2026-09-17

verdict: No JavaScript-free route to Google results survives: every JS-free shape is refused (/sorry or 403) and every 200 is the application shell with zero results in the HTML. Results require JS, and with JS the per-search challenge rejects our sessions. The 'persistent profile / session age' idea is refuted at its source: real logged-in session cookies stopped working in July because the challenge is re-run per search rather than trusted per session. Do not build anti-detection work on that premise.
